newsitem.title: GERMANY: No sign of crash for German shares despite wobble.
newsitem.headline: No sign of crash for German shares despite wobble.

text.p: German shares still look set to rise and rise despite a wobble on Thursday as investors took profits on surging bank stocks, dealers said.
"If this was the consolidation, and it might just be, it's nothing," said a Frankfurt dealer.
A Stuttgart dealer said: "A crash just isn't on the cards. Fundamentals apart, the fact is institutions are still putting their money in this market."
The IBIS DAX index was up 1.02 points at 4,385.02 points at 1308 GMT, some 50 points ahead of the bourse session close, which the DAX closed down 1.6 percent.
September DAX futures were up one point at 4,421 points.
Dealers were drawing breath after a day which saw the IBIS DAX veer more than 100 points from a new record high of 4,449.33 points to a low of 4,334 points.
The lows came as investors took profits on bank stocks, the greatest winner of the past few days amid a fresh bout of speculation about mergers in the sector.

But the market was also buoyed by factors such as the strong dollar, which traded at close to 1.84 marks in the afternoon, heralding even higher returns for Germany's export-driven car, chemical and engineering industries.
Vereinsbank hit lows of 95 marks during the day but pared its losses to trade at 106 marks, down 4.9 percent in late dealings.
The bank had issued a slightly below-expectations earnings report for the first six months of 1997 in the morning.
Commerzbank AG was down 1.50 marks at 63.10 marks.
Vereinsbank reported operating profit of 498.5 million marks for the first half while Commerzbank posted operating profit of 1.63 billion, just above forecasts.
Dealers downplayed the fall in bank shares, saying the sector was likely to recover fast.

Analysts pointed out that merger speculation was the driving force behind bank share gains, not earnings news, and that speculation is certain to persist after Vereinsbank announced plans to merge with Hypo-bank on Monday.
The winners of the day included engineering giant Siemens AG which was up 5.45 marks at 124.60 marks in afternoon trade.
Dealers said there was no fundamental reason for Siemens' gains, but that investors were still seeking for bargains in a market where prices ar almost uniformly at all-time highs.
